headline: Cape Verde holds Uruguay to a 2-2 draw, strengthening knockout stage hopes after stunning Spain
summary: Cape Verde continues its surprising run in the World Cup, securing a crucial draw against Uruguay after previously holding Euro champions Spain to a goalless tie. Their strong performance puts them in a solid position for the knockout rounds.
details: Cape Verde continued their impressive World Cup campaign by holding Uruguay to a 2-2 draw, following their goalless tie against Euro champions Spain. This result strengthens their position in the race for the knockout stages.

Cape Verde took the lead in the 21st minute when Kevin Pina scored from a free-kick after Telmo Arcanjo was fouled. This historic goal marked Cape Verde's first-ever goal in the World Cup main tournament.
Uruguay equalized before halftime with a header from Maxi Araujo, capitalizing on a rebound. Agustin Canobbio then put Uruguay ahead 2-1, scoring from another opportunity created by Araujo's header.

Helio Varela, coming on as a substitute in the second half, quickly brought Cape Verde level just two minutes later. He seized on a weak backpass from Uruguayan defender Matias Olivera, drawing the goalkeeper out and slotting the ball into an empty net.
Following this draw, both Uruguay and Cape Verde now have two points each in Group H. Spain currently leads the group with four points, setting up an exciting final round of matches.
caption:

headline: Iraq's Arnold promises to have a go against France at World Cup clash
summary: Ranked 57th, Iraq faces tournament favourites France in their second World Cup match, with coach Graham Arnold vowing an attacking approach despite their previous loss to Norway.
details: Iraq coach Graham Arnold declared his team will play to win against tournament favourites France in their upcoming World Cup clash. He emphasized a winning mentality, stating his team will not simply try to avoid defeat.
The Group I encounter is set to take place in Philadelphia. Iraq, ranked 57th globally, is participating in their first World Cup since 1986 after a rigorous 21-match qualifying campaign.

Their World Cup journey began with a 4-1 loss to Erling Haaland's Norway in Boston. Now, they face the formidable task of containing France's superstar attack, led by captain Kylian Mbappe, who scored twice in Les Bleus' 3-1 victory over Senegal.

Arnold light-heartedly remarked about needing three goalkeepers to handle France's threat, but affirmed his team's focus on their own performance. He confirmed winger Ali Jasim is fit to start, though the decision on captain Jalal Hassan's goalkeeping position is still pending.

The 62-year-old coach, who took charge of the Lions of Mesopotamia last May, expressed anticipation for measuring himself against France's Didier Deschamps. Deschamps is set to step down after 14 years, making this his final World Cup.
